snippet.textDisplay:
Nah, that's an insane take. No way should a team (that's better before an injury) be counted differently than the same team after an injury. Absolutely insane.

First, do we even understand how many players are out for injuries week in and week out? Across all college football? And you think ANYONE is going to judge a team completely different if they lose a future 1st round offensive lineman out for a game? Hell, no.

Secondly if the entire team the rest of the season is a "shell of itself" because ONE GUY is out, you didn't have a good team, you had a crutch. If you go from an 11-1 team to a 5-7 team because of one guy.... The team is cooked. That means there's NO DEPTH, lack of coaching, no team synergy, on and on.

Lastly, if we're accepting that we're judging performance based off of PERCEIVED individual talent, then how the hell are we saying we're not factoring "power rankings" in to this? Because the guy who plays 3-4 games a season sure as hell doesn't have the actual resume to show they're for real - that somehow they're unlike any other star athlete across any other programs that have had time to watch tape and and game plan around them.

The only fair way I see to rate these games is to look at ACTUAL resume. Tough luck that you might have had a little tougher of a game against an opponent compared to someone else, but that's football. That team lacked depth most of all, but also coaching to make things work after an injury.

snippet.textDisplay: I said this the first year of the CFP rankings. They should have done away with the Preseason/AP poll. If the CFP said they didn't have enough body of work from each team until week 8/9 to do an accurate ranking. snippet.textDisplay: Alabama shouldn’t be #5 but Tennessee shouldn’t be ranked ahead of them either. Tennessee hasn’t beaten the same level of teams as Bama, judgement on Tennessee isn’t based solely on the Bama Win. Bama beat #6 Kentucky 45-17, #21 South Carolina 49-18, Mississippi State 56-23 (Ranked #16 and with a healthy Kamario Taylor) and loss to #2 Georgia by 3. Tennessee’s overall resume doesn’t match that and beating Bama alone doesn’t make their resume equivalent. A Head to Head win is only going to be the deciding factor if both teams have equal resumes like Miami and ND last year but this isn’t that. Bama hasn’t played any FCS schools and Tennessee has played 2, other than the Bama Win…Tennessee’s best win is 4-4 Auburn. This committee has made it clear they’re judging each separately based on who they’ve played and beaten which is the way it should be.

snippet.textDisplay: For the first time since I began watching college football, the playoff committee has demonstrated genuine common sense in their selections. I completely agree with their decisions, particularly regarding Alabama's placement. The committee showed excellent judgment by factoring in the context of Alabama's hard-fought loss to Georgia—a game where many felt officiating heavily influenced the outcome. The physical toll of that matchup was evident the following week when both severely depleted teams lost their subsequent games while missing multiple key starters. The committee rightfully accounted for that attrition and also gave Alabama well-deserved credit for defeating a strong Mississippi State team that was still operating at full capacity with its starting quarterback. Finally, Notre Dame is ranked exactly where they belong, accurately reflecting the weakness of their schedule.

Make the playoff based mostly on conference results:
1st and 2nd place teams from each P4 conference gets a first round bye and home field in the 2nd round. (8 out of the 24).
3rd and 4th place teams from the P4 plus the next 8 available committee ranked teams play each other in the 1st round. Make 2 of those 8 from the group of whatever and independents. Let the committee set the brackets/seeding.
Takes away all these arguments except for who the bottom 8 teams will be. Each P4 automatically gets 4 teams in.

snippet.textDisplay:
These rankings need to be seen in the context of what the committee is building a foundation for.  There is lots more football to play, but the point is that the committee wants to shape the narrative of what those games mean.  Notre Dame's ranking is perhaps the most obvious example.  The committee is clearly saying that BYU was the one mulligan.  Win the rest of the way and Notre Dame is in.  But one more loss and they can eat pop tarts.  

And 5 SEC teams in the playoffs right now is just placeholders as the circular firing squad will continue.  The important thing is that the remaining games are conference games and regardless of which SEC team loses, an SEC team will also get a good win.  They are stating how they think the spots get divvied up among the conferences.  SEC still gets 5.  B12 might get 2, but it will be at the expense of the B1G (who now only gets 2).  And frankly, that seems reasonable as no B1G team has looked great.  ACC only gets 1.  Of course, some things can throw a wrench in it.  If Utah wins out and wins the conference championship, it will be easy to make them the sole B12 bid.  If Miami loses the ACC championship (after going undefeated in the regular season), ACC probably gets 2. But if that happens, ND lost and the second ACC slot maybe comes at the expense of ND.  

Also, if you want to evaluate wins based on pre-injury status, you also have to consider injuries in the rankings.  Ohio State is on the outside looking in because Sayin is injured.  If OSU can show that it can win big games without him, maybe they get a shot.  But the pre-injury record won't be enough.

snippet.textDisplay:
Not to show bias, but Indiana has found a way to win with a hurt QB and a beat up roster. This bye week was needed, big time. Hoover has not shown us great stuff over the last 4 weeks, but hes hurt. Im glad for the bye week and Im super happy I got tickets to that thriller with the Gophers. People who did not pay attention to that game will say whatever they want to discredit the W, but IU beat the crap out of the Gophers statistically. And I know stats only mean so much.. but they do show something. The Gophers REALLY struggled to run the ball which made Drakes life hell. And special teams KILLED IU, but the Gophers scored 1 touchdown on a trick play and otherwise, could not move the ball consistently at all. We did move the ball all game, even with a hurt QB, but redzone play was bad and our special teams had a meltdown. And this being a game of inches, Shazz almost had a TD but HARDLY bobbled the ball. Correct call, he was out. Jacob Savage (True freshman BTW, played out of his mind all game) almost had a game sealing interception but was ruled an incomplete pass.

One thing I do know, Cig will iron this out. Not many teams have that much confidence in their coach, we do. Also, having a backup QB with a set of STONES on him that can sling the ball the way Wilson did is nice. Every snap that kids confidence skyrocketed and you could see it. Im not arguing for or against the placement, what I am saying is, the mark of a champion is finding a way to win, no matter what. Close games with good teams may not be sexy.. last week was UGLY for IU, but they found a way to win. And that is the DNA of Cignetti, just find a way to win.

snippet.textDisplay: ​@TheSeanburke101 You mean, like the #1 team in the country Miami or another top 10 team, BYU?  I am not saying they are deserving of a top 3 or even top 5 spot as of right now, but 11 is too low. If you take their whole body of work compared to all the other teams, they should be somewhere in the top 10. Notre Dame is #1 in margin of victory and average scoring margin nationally. That is a big deal. They are #4 in game control and ranked #1 in Sagarin's, #1 in ESPN FPI (football power index), they are #1 in FEI ratings, #4 in scoring defense and # 3 in turnover margin. They are up there at the top. You have to consider everything. The whole resume and body of work. Notre Dame's only loss came to a top 10 team, on the road in a hostile environment, in only a 4-point loss in what was once again, an extremely controversial loss. People act like Notre Dame just gets dominated in these games. All the way back to last year in their only loses, they are all down to the last second games, in which there were bad calls or highly questionable calls, along with coming down to the last play at the last second. Then there only loss this year was to BYU, and it was not only controversial, but they flat out got screwed because evidence shows that there was still a second left on the clock and they should have gotten a chance to run another play inside the 10-yard line and it should have been pass interference as well. Officials have said the same thing after the game. All these same things have to be taken into account. Then they have pretty much dominated in margin of victory in all of their other games in which they won. They dominated a 5-3 Wisconsin team that dominated USC. They beat both Stanford and North Carolina by a larger margin than the #1 team Miami did. Indiana hasn't beaten anybody to be that high and they lost a close one to Ohio State and they are at #4? There are teams like Alabama and Texas who have not only 2 loses but have also looked bad in a lot of their other games too, wins included. I mean, Alabama lost 26-10 to Tennessee. I mean, could you imagine if Notre Dame lost 26-10 to BYU? I guess because it's Alabama they get a pass though, right? Or when Texas plays Ohio State, they are always supposed to be rewarded for playing tough competition, but when Notre Dame plays #1 Miami or #7 BYU there is no mention of the same standard of playing tough competition. No matter who Notre Dame plays, all we ever hear about is Notre Dame has a weak schedule, no matter who they play, it always works against them somehow, but when it comes to certain teams like Alabama, Texas or even Ohio State, it's always they need to be rewarded for playing a tough top 10 opponent and that is my issue, the double standards and inconsistences across the board! The hypocrisy, double standards and inconsistencies is my major problem, and it is devaluing this great sport! So, my biggest issue is the inconsistencies and hypocrisy with the committee and the positioning of all the teams. Now, if Notre Dame loses to Miami, you won't hear much from me, but I am just talking about up until this point, they should be higher than 11 and we all know how they got completely gaslighted and screwed over last year too. There is a lot of good games this weekend. I just want fairness and consistency with all of the teams. God Bless you!!

snippet.textDisplay: I hope I live to see the day where they chop off about 80 teams from the FBS. Those teams have zero chance to win a title so what’s the point? Top 2 teams from each division make a playoff. Maybe 2 or 4 wildcards and be done with it. You play every team in your division once a season in a home and away rotation every other year. You still have 3 or 4 out of division games to schedule old rivalry games that may have unfortunately got broken up by division alignment. Or schedule whoever ya want. Toss in some sort of relegation system from the current league of 60 and the other 80 some teams that didn’t make the big league cut. Perfection. No more bs polls. No more cupcake schedules. Far less meaningless 63-3 blowout games vs bottom feeder teams.

snippet.textDisplay:
Remember a few weeks ago when all the Sankey politicking for more Strength of Schedule resulted in the committee making a statement that they would give more weight to SoS than last year? 

Result: SEC schools got a good boost and weak schedulers like Notre Dame got busted down. 

Based on this new factor, the rankings make perfect sense. 

What doesn't make sense is that Sankey was able to throw his weight around with the committee and win because there's massive parity now among these top 25 teams and the idea that the SEC has that much more ridiculously difficult conference schedule is not as justified as it's been in previous years. 

While conferences like the big 12 are about six or seven deep with quality teams.

snippet.textDisplay:
Three-loss SEC teams in the College Football Playoff? Are you kidding me?!

If this doesn’t expose the blatant bias in the playoff selection process, I don’t know what will! At what point do we stop rewarding teams simply because they play in the SEC?

Let’s call a spade a spade: The SEC isn’t nearly as dominant as the media, rankings, and selection committee want everyone to believe.

It’s time to reward teams for what they actually accomplish on the field, not for the conference logo on their jerseys.

Conference reputation shouldn’t outweigh results. This is SEC bias at its finest!

snippet.textDisplay:
@synitarthrax5618 Never thought about it this way - that's a great take. I'm a huge soccer fan. All the big European leagues have tiers. The top league just plays each other, and so on. Worst performers in the top league are relegated and best performers in lower leagues jump to higher leagues. It's really interesting because it means teams at the bottom have a lot at stake and their games matter a TON beyond just the coaching carousel we see in American sports.

ND joins a conference (for their own good, play quality teams and they can show off their strength), G6 has the tier two NCAA playoffs which is fun b/c now we get two championships, and then it helps the SEC mess happening right now get fixed because it's no longer about beating out 10-1 schools in other conferences with weaker resumes, they just have to beat more of the SEC teams. And then finally - we will know which conference is superior hahaha. Just my thoughts on your idea, I think its great.

Part of the problem with college football is we have too many polls with differing philosophies and die hard traditions that are being used alongside a playoff system. I don’t want to hear about power conferences, strength of schedule, blah blah blah. College football is a joke. It is the only major sport in America where your record is not the primary determining factor of your seeding. The way it SHOULD work is 1. Miami, 2. Utah, and 3. UCLA (or shuffle the seedings of these three). Then everyone else is arranged by record. 1 loss teams are ranked next, then 2 loss teams, etc. No committees. No boosters influence. No back door deals. Let these young men play. Line up, strap it on and play. Strength of schedule, etc should only come into play AFTER you are presented with a situation where you have, for example, two undefeated teams and have to decide how to compare them, and them alone, to one another. Oh, you’re Alabama but lost 2 games? Sorry, you are out of the conversation, you’re not undefeated.

snippet.textDisplay:
It's easy to make a case for them being underrated at #5 if you actually use your brain and look at all the Teams closely instead of acting like an AP voter who just goes off Wins & Losses. You have to actually do a little work by looking at schedules/opponents schedules/results & scores/(this one is Rare, usually only 1 or 2 of these type situations per season but a season altering injury to a player who is super dynamic who completely changes a team(Mississippi State is a great example & only team at moment who fits this category, hard to include Ohio State given how talented the roster is top to bottom)/ check this component with each team you are evaluating.

If you do all the work like I just said and properly evaluate each Team, you can't find a team with a better resume than Alabama outside of maybe Utah, Miami, Georgia and all 3 are stretching it to be higher. Especially Georgia. A case for Tennessee could be accepted but the Home Loss to Texas and Loss to South Carolina drops them below Alabama and puts Tennessee at #6 and I've got Kentucky at #5. It's hard to put Kentucky over Alabama when they got blown by them At Home 45-17. I think Notre Dame is very good and could be better but it's hard to show it with the pathetic schedule they play and lack of any Quality Wins.
Some will argue Texas is close but the Oklahoma Loss really really hurts considering Oklahoma has Lost to Michigan, Lost AT HOME to Kentucky, just got blown out At Home to South Carolina. Albeit South Carolina and Kentucky are both probably Top 12 Teams themselves. The Texas Loss AT HOME to Florida hurts a lot too. Florida got blown out by Missouri and AT HOME to South Carolina.
